style.vernacular: Small, dusty tropical port capital of whitewashed and pastel-painted render. Portuguese colonial buildings of 1-2 storeys with arcaded verandas, shutters and red clay-tile roofs sit along the seafront grid; Indonesian-era (1975-99) concrete-block and brick buildings with flat or low-pitched corrugated-metal roofs fill the rest; recent donor-built concrete blocks and mall-style buildings stand in the centre. Outside Dili, villages use block walls with corrugated-iron roofs, and in places wooden houses. Dry savanna vegetation with palms, tamarind and fig trees.
style.ornament: Portuguese colonial arcaded verandas, shutters and turrets (Palacio de Lahane, Government Palace with three two-storey blocks linked by an arcade); Indonesian-era concrete screens and Catholic churches with bell towers and porticos; Balinese split gates (candi bentar) and tiered meru roofs on the Hindu temple; Timorese uma lulik pitched roofs as local motif.
